key_insight: The paper shows that diffusion-style motion planning can be done without training by using analytical local scores from nearby obstacles, smoothness, velocity, and agent interactions.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical trajectory planning for complex, multi-robot systems when demonstrations are scarce, while preserving smooth, collision-free behavior and fast iterative refinement.
method: Replace learned global trajectory scores with analytical local scores computed from local waypoint/constraint interactions.
Use decomposed denoising to iteratively refine trajectories while maintaining classical optimization structure.
Model feasibility through obstacle, smoothness, velocity, and inter-agent terms for multi-agent planning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful large-scale experiments, including feasible paths for 300+ agents amid 100+ obstacles in under 6 seconds on a GPU, outperforming strong learning-based and optimization baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the analytical local score design and local constraint modeling, so difficult geometries or missing terms could reduce feasibility.
paper_title: Training-Free Diffusion Planning with Analytical Local Scores
